t: For necessary expenses for the acquisition, construction, commissioning, and upgrading of major research equipment, facilities, and other such capital assets pursuant to the National Science Foundation Act of 1950 (42 U.S.C. 1861 et seq.), including authorized travel, $196,170,000, to remain available until expended:  Provided, That none of the funds may be used to reimburse the Judgment Fund established under section 1304 of title 31, United States Code.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision funding NSF major research equipment and facilities, with a restriction on reimbursing the Judgment Fund. The tempting reading is that the reference to the Judgment Fund implies litigation against the government, but it only limits the use of funds and grants no outside party a right to sue or any consultative role. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: For necessary expenses for the acquisition, construction, commissioning, and upgrading of major research equipment, facilities, and other such capital assets

opus.w: This is an appropriation for National Science Foundation research equipment and facilities. It provides no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or consultation with anyone outside the federal government. The mention of the Judgment Fund might look like it touches on litigation, but it only limits how the money can be spent. It does not give an outside party any right to sue over a federal decision.
opus.s: Provided, That none of the funds may be used to reimburse the Judgment Fund established under section 1304 of title 31, United States Code.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes the expenditure of funds for specific capital assets. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. The reference to the National Science Foundation Act is merely to identify the statutory authority for the expenses, not to invoke participation mechanisms within that Act.
qwen_chat.s: For necessary expenses for the acquisition, construction, commissioning, and upgrading of major research equipment, facilities, and other such capital assets pursuant to the National Science Foundation Act of 1950 (42 U.S.C. 1861 et seq.), including authorized travel, $196,170,000, to remain available until expended: Provided, That none of the funds may be used to reimburse the Judgment Fund established under section 1304 of title 31, United States Code.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the reference to the "National Science Foundation Act of 1950" implies participation because that Act might contain participation provisions. However, this specific section is merely an appropriations clause authorizing the expenditure of funds for capital assets. It does not itself establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties. The restriction on reimbursing the Judgment Fund is a financial constraint, not a participation mechanism.
